subject: brown tree snake
title: What If a Snake Took Over an Island? Guam Has 2 Million of Them

scenes.text: What if one snake species took over a whole island? Guam found out, and the forest went silent.
Around 1950, a few brown tree snakes arrived in cargo. Guam had nothing that ate snakes.
By the 1980s, 10 of the island's 12 native forest birds were gone. Eaten, eggs and all.
Today about 2 million snakes live on 200 square miles. The densest snake population on Earth.
They climb power lines and short them out. In 2025 Guam logged 44 snake blackouts, one every eight days.
With no birds to carry seeds, 90 percent now drop at the parent tree. The forest itself is stopping. One snake did that.

description:
What if a snake took over an island? On Guam it happened: brown tree snakes arrived in cargo around 1950 and now number about 2 million.
They wiped out 10 of 12 native forest bird species, cause dozens of power outages a year, and, with no birds to carry seeds, forest regrowth is expected to fall 61 to 92 percent.
